messages:
cate: quick flag 1: ran into a parity + retry issue between node/python sampleapps on embeddings/rerank. node batch helper produced a short final vector and server returned 400 vector_dim_mismatch. sampleapp retried and we saw duplicate inserts.

allen: can you paste the small repro? might be off-by-one when slicing Float32 buffers or a base64 trim in our test harness.

cate: minimal repro (node):
```js
const raw = Buffer.concat(vecs.map(v => Buffer.from(new Float32Array(v).buffer)));
const body = { model: 'redwood-embed-001', data: raw.toString('base64') };
fetch('/v1/embeddings', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(body) });
```

nina: saw similar earlier. two fixes: client-side preflight validation (reject or opt-in pad/truncate) and tighten sampleapp retry rules so structural 4xx aren't auto-retried.

cate: i used padShort(vecs, dim) locally to unblock tests but that hides the root cause. prefer strict validation by default.

allen: propose JS SDK config: `vectorValidation: { mode: 'strict'|'pad'|'truncate' }` default strict, and SDK throws before network. will open PR.

nina: also noticed rerank response shape drift: python wrapper returns objects with explicit ids, node sometimes returns array-only. normalize SDK to always attach ids. that will make dedupe robust after retries.

ops: heads-up 1: retry-induced duplicates may inflate billing. tagging finance to audit recent spikes. :money_with_wings: 

ci-bot: opened PR #912 by allen: "js-sdk: add vectorValidation option (strict|pad|truncate); sampleapp: narrow 4xx retry list" 1: checks queued.

cate: i'll add a tiny integration test in sampleapp that runs node+python against a local embed server and asserts vector lengths + response ids match. include fuzz for base64 vs JSON array paths.

allen: also adding server-side error hint `retryable:false` for structural validation errors so clients with broad retry rules can still behave correctly. filing server RFC.

nina: nice. once PR passes we should roll sampleapp patch and add CI matrix test to prevent regressions. thanks for quick triage. :rocket:
